name: FRANCE
lead: France is the largest country in the EU. Snowy Alps meet sunflower fields. Visitors come to see the Eiffel Tower, eat croissants and walk through vineyards.

sections.wows: 7 things to make you go wow

geo: France looks almost like a hexagon (a six-sided shape). The north has flat farmland and chalk cliffs above the Channel. The Loire and Seine rivers wind past châteaux (castles).
The Alps rise along the east. Mont Blanc is the highest peak in Western Europe. In the middle sits the Massif Central, an ancient volcanic plateau.
animals: Forests shelter red deer, wild boar and shy roe deer. Golden eagles soar above the Pyrenees. Flamingos wade through the shallow Camargue lagoons in the south.
The Camargue also has wild white horses. Otters have returned to mountain streams. Lynx hunt quietly in the Vosges forests.
culture: France gave the world impressionist painting, cinema and haute couture (fancy fashion). Cinema was invented in Lyon in 1895.
A law says a true baguette must be baked fresh on site. France has over 1,200 named cheeses. The French eat about 26 kg of cheese each per year.
history: Celtic Gauls lived in France before Julius Caesar conquered it in 52 BC. In 1429, teenage Joan of Arc rallied the French army. Her victories helped end the Hundred Years' War.
The 1789 Revolution toppled the king. It spread the idea that people should rule themselves. Napoleon conquered much of Europe before his defeat in 1815. In 1944, Allied forces freed Paris.
wows: About 90 million tourists visit France a year, more than its whole population.
The Eiffel Tower was due to be torn down after 1889, yet is now the world's most-visited paid monument.
French territory touches the Atlantic, Pacific and Indian Oceans, and even borders Brazil.
A French law makes bakers take turns on holiday, so every area has fresh bread.
Tour de France riders cycle about 3,400 km in 3 weeks.
Camargue flamingos hatch grey and turn pink from eating algae and shrimp.
France has won more Nobel Prizes in Literature than any other nation.

myths.fact: The croissant's ancestor, the kipferl, came from Austria. French bakers later made it flaky and famous.
Napoleon was about 1.69 m tall, average for his time. French inches were longer than English ones.
